key_insight: BenchX shows that AI tumor-detection models can look strong overall but fail sharply in specific demographic and imaging subgroups.
clinical_relevance: Subgroup-level testing is essential in medical imaging because real-world performance gaps may affect which patients are reliably detected and which are missed.
method: Built an open benchmark from 85,355 CT scans.
Evaluated 12 tumor-detection AI models across tumor size, location, patient subgroup, and imaging protocol.
Used LLMs to extract and organize subgroup information from clinical data for scalable, reproducible analysis.
evidence_signal: The benchmark found that state-of-the-art models optimized for average accuracy performed poorly in rare or underrepresented groups, including young, female African Americans.
watch_item: Because rare subgroups have limited annotated data, results may highlight gaps that are difficult to fix quickly and should not be overgeneralized beyond the benchmark settings.
paper_title: BenchX: Benchmarking AI Models for Cancer Detection and Localization with Demographic and Protocol Biases
